text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B uses varied sentence structures with subordinate clauses like 'so even is not there season they still have to condition and train' and 'due to the fact that they have homework to do'", "quality": "Syntactic complexity", "description": "The essay combines multiple clauses and ideas within sentences, showing more advanced control over sentence construction than the short, fragmented sentences of Essay A."}, {"evidence": "Essay B develops multiple distinct reasons (jobs, stress, extracurriculars, tutoring) each with elaboration, while Essay A repeats the same few points", "quality": "Argument development", "description": "The essay sustains and elaborates several separate supporting points rather than circling back to the same claims."}, {"evidence": "Essay B uses cohesive transitions like 'Another reason why', 'One other major reason is that', and 'My conclusion is that'", "quality": "Organizational structure", "description": "The essay signals its structure with explicit transitional phrases that guide the reader through the argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay B spells most words correctly and uses more conventional grammar, e.g., 'attend those classes required to graduate', compared to Essay A's pervasive misspellings like 'estreced', 'enought', 'beneficts', 'chool'", "quality": "Spelling and grammatical accuracy", "description": "The essay shows far fewer spelling and grammatical errors, indicating stronger control over written English conventions."}, {"evidence": "Essay B uses academic vocabulary such as 'higher education', 'community college', 'work force', 'extra curricular activity', 'volunteering in the community'", "quality": "Academic vocabulary range", "description": "The essay draws on a broader and more formal vocabulary appropriate to persuasive writing."}]}
